description: Repo with two Nygard-format ADRs and meeting notes choosing a PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED job table over RabbitMQ/Redis; a correct answer writes ADR 0003 in the same format, links ADR 0002, and updates the index.

adr-author.task: The project in `{fixture}/` keeps ADRs in `{fixture}/docs/adr/`. Record the background-jobs decision described in `{fixture}/decision-notes.md` as a new ADR and update the ADR index. If the `adr` CLI is unavailable, follow the existing numbering, file naming, and format by hand. Nobody will review this interactively, so leave the status for a human to accept. The grader cannot open files: end your answer with the full text of every file you created or changed under `{fixture}/docs/adr/`, each preceded by its path.

rubricPoints.requirement: The new ADR is file `docs/adr/0003-<kebab-title>.md` with an H1 of the form `# 3. <Title>`, a `Date:` line, and `## Status`, `## Context`, `## Decision`, `## Consequences` sections like ADRs 0001 and 0002.

The ADR records the decision to use a PostgreSQL job table claimed with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, and names RabbitMQ and Redis as rejected alternatives with the reason (a new stateful system to operate).
The Context states the forcing problem: duplicate emails from two cron hosts picking the same row and/or the month-end backlog of the polling cron script.
The ADR references ADR 0002 (PostgreSQL as the only datastore) as the decision it builds on.
`docs/adr/README.md` gains an entry linking `0003-...md`, and the ADR's status is Proposed (not Accepted).
